title: Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale)

spark.summary: Architect a Netflix-scale global video streaming platform separating a cloud Control Plane from ISP-embedded Open Connect CDN appliances and a distributed Transcoding DAG.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, keep 100% of heavy video bytes on ISP-embedded edge CDN appliances via proactive overnight pre-positioning, while the cloud Control Plane handles auth, manifests, and traffic steering.
spark.byteSummary:
Serving 250M+ subscribers streaming 4K video simultaneously cannot run through centralized cloud origin servers—transatlantic egress alone would saturate backbone links and cost billions.

The architecture splits cleanly into three planes: (1) an Ingestion & Transcoding DAG that converts studio mezzanine masters into CENC-encrypted ABR segments in S3; (2) an ISP-embedded Open Connect Edge CDN that caches popular titles inside local ISPs via overnight BGP-aware pre-positioning; and (3) a cloud Control Plane.

When a user presses Play, the cloud Playback Service authenticates entitlements, consults real-time CDN health telemetry, and returns a signed manifest pointing directly to the 3 nearest healthy Open Connect appliances.

learningJourney.title: Control Plane (Cloud) vs. Data Plane (ISP Edge CDN)
learningJourney.purpose: Keep 99%+ of video bytes inside local ISPs while running business logic in elastic cloud regions.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Control Plane (Cloud) vs. Data Plane (ISP Edge CDN)** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale): Keep 99%+ of video bytes inside local ISPs while running business logic in elastic cloud regions.
explanation.core: Control-plane requests (login, browse, bookmark sync, play-button manifest) are tiny JSON payloads (<10 KB) suited for multi-region cloud microservices. Data-plane traffic (video segments) is massive (15+ Mbps per stream) and must terminate inside local ISP/IXP Open Connect appliances so bytes travel one hop.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, control plane (cloud) vs. data plane (isp edge cdn) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Global streaming architecture with VMAF per-title DAGs, CENC multi-DRM, stateless edge HMAC auth, and closed-loop Flink QoE steering.

learningJourney.title: Studio Mezzanine Ingest & Distributed Transcoding Pipeline
learningJourney.purpose: Ingest multi-terabyte raw studio masters reliably and orchestrate parallel ABR encoding.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Studio Mezzanine Ingest & Distributed Transcoding Pipeline** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale): Ingest multi-terabyte raw studio masters reliably and orchestrate parallel ABR encoding.
explanation.core: Studios upload multi-terabyte IMF/ProRes masters via resumable multipart uploads to S3. An Ingestion Orchestrator validates frame checksums, extracts audio/subtitle tracks, and triggers the GOP-parallel Transcoding DAG + CENC packager, writing immutable ABR segments to regional S3 origins.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, studio mezzanine ingest & distributed transcoding pipeline becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Global streaming architecture with VMAF per-title DAGs, CENC multi-DRM, stateless edge HMAC auth, and closed-loop Flink QoE steering.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, keep 100% of heavy video bytes on ISP-embedded edge CDN appliances via proactive overnight pre-positioning, while the cloud Control Plane handles auth, manifests, and traffic steering.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale) experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Proactive Overnight Pre-Positioning vs. Reactive Pull
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate cold-cache origin storms on major new releases using popularity-predicted overnight fills.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Proactive Overnight Pre-Positioning vs. Reactive Pull** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale): Eliminate cold-cache origin storms on major new releases using popularity-predicted overnight fills.
explanation.core: If 20 million subscribers hit Play on a Friday premiere simultaneously, reactive CDN cache-miss pulls would crush the S3 origin. Instead, a Popularity Predictor pushes new releases and top-ranked catalog titles to Open Connect appliances during off-peak overnight hours (2 AM–6 AM local time) via BGP-aware filling.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, proactive overnight pre-positioning vs. reactive pull becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Global streaming architecture with VMAF per-title DAGs, CENC multi-DRM, stateless edge HMAC auth, and closed-loop Flink QoE steering.

learningJourney.title: Real-Time GSLB & Telemetry-Driven Traffic Steering
learningJourney.purpose: Route around overloaded CDN nodes or congested ISP peering links in real time.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Real-Time GSLB & Telemetry-Driven Traffic Steering** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale): Route around overloaded CDN nodes or congested ISP peering links in real time.
explanation.core: Open Connect appliances emit heartbeats every few seconds reporting NIC saturation, disk queue depth, and TCP retransmit rates. When a node exceeds 85% NIC utilization, the Traffic Router dynamically shifts new Playback Service manifest URLs to neighboring healthy appliances or secondary IXP caches.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, real-time gslb & telemetry-driven traffic steering becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Global streaming architecture with VMAF per-title DAGs, CENC multi-DRM, stateless edge HMAC auth, and closed-loop Flink QoE steering.

learningJourney.title: High-Write Viewing History & Continue-Watching State
learningJourney.purpose: Absorb millions of concurrent playback heartbeats (`position_sec`) without overwhelming OLTP DBs.

explanation.foundation: 250M devices sending a playback-position heartbeat every 30 seconds generates >8M writes/sec.
explanation.core: Writing every heartbeat to a relational DB fails.
explanation.deepDive: Heartbeats ingest through Kafka/Flink into a write-optimized Cassandra/RocksDB store partitioned by `(profile_id, title_id)` with TTLs on granular logs and compact `last_position` snapshots.

cards.label: LWW Timestamping
cards.detail: Cassandra `USING TIMESTAMP` prevents out-of-order heartbeats from rewinding progress.

cards.label: Client Debounce
cards.detail: Players always flush a final heartbeat on Pause/Exit.

sectionDiagram.summary: Coalescing heartbeats into timestamped Cassandra writes scales Continue Watching to 8M+ QPS.
sectionDiagram.caption: Kafka + Cassandra with client timestamps absorb millions of playback heartbeats per second.

learningJourney.title: Live Sports & Global Premiere Thundering-Herd Protection
learningJourney.purpose: Survive 20M simultaneous viewers joining a live boxing match or season premiere at 8:00 PM.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Live Sports & Global Premiere Thundering-Herd Protection** as the intuition layer for Design a Global Video Streaming & Transcoding Platform (Netflix Scale): Survive 20M simultaneous viewers joining a live boxing match or season premiere at 8:00 PM.
explanation.core: Unlike on-demand movies, live events create a synchronized thundering herd at T=00:00 and require low-latency CMAF chunked transfer (`LL-HLS`/`LL-DASH`) plus jittered client startup, tokenized edge authentication (signed URLs verified locally on the edge with HMAC, zero origin round-trip), and degraded-mode static fallback manifests.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, live sports & global premiere thundering-herd protection becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Global streaming architecture with VMAF per-title DAGs, CENC multi-DRM, stateless edge HMAC auth, and closed-loop Flink QoE steering.

learningJourney.title: Real-Time QoE Telemetry & Automated Anomaly Rollback
learningJourney.purpose: Detect ISP peering degradation or bad codec deployments within 60 seconds via player QoE beacons.

explanation.foundation: CDN edge metrics alone miss last-mile Wi-Fi or player-decoder crashes.
explanation.core: Every client emits compact QoE beacons (`startup_ms`, `rebuffer_ratio`, `avg_bitrate`, `cdn_node_id`).
explanation.deepDive: Streaming aggregations in Flink/Druid alert within 60 seconds if a specific ISP ASN or new app build spikes rebuffering, triggering automated traffic steering away from affected edges.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does Netflix deploy Open Connect CDN appliances directly inside local ISPs rather than serving all 4K video from AWS S3?

options.text: S3 cannot store files larger than 100 MB.
options.feedback: S3 supports objects up to 5 TB.

options.text: Serving petabits of video from central cloud regions would saturate internet backbone peering and incur massive egress costs.
options.feedback: Correct! ISP-embedded appliances keep >99% of video traffic local to the ISP's last-mile network.

options.text: Open Connect appliances run the recommendation ML models.
options.feedback: Recommendations run in the cloud Control Plane; Open Connect serves video bytes.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Co-locating video caches inside ISPs eliminates backbone transit bottlenecks and cuts egress costs dramatically.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does overnight proactive pre-positioning prevent origin overload on major Friday title premieres?

options.text: It blocks users from watching until Monday.
It pushes predicted hit titles to ISP edge disks during off-peak 2-6 AM hours before prime-time traffic arrives.
options.feedback: Correct! Warming edge caches off-peak yields >98% cache hit rates during prime time.
All ABR rungs including 4K are pre-positioned.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Off-peak predictive filling utilizes free overnight ISP capacity so prime-time streams hit warm local disks.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the Playback Service return 3 ranked CDN edge URLs inside the manifest instead of relying solely on DNS GSLB?

options.feedback: DNS supports both IPv4 and IPv6.

options.text: Manifest-level URLs bypass stale DNS TTLs and let the client fail over to Edge #2 immediately on a 503.
options.feedback: Correct! Client-side failover across 3 pre-selected edge URLs recovers in milliseconds without waiting for DNS expiry.

options.text: Browsers cannot resolve DNS for video files.
options.feedback: Browsers resolve DNS normally, but DNS caching delays failover.

options.text: To play 3 different movies at once.
options.feedback: The 3 URLs are replicas of the same title.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Embedding multiple ranked edge URLs in the playback manifest enables instant client-side failover.
